rows.name: Targa Resources
rows.thesis: Fee-based gas gathering and processing that grows with Permian volumes; it is near its high and steadier than the refiners.
rows.risks: It carries the most leverage of my holdings (net debt 31% of mcap), and Permian volumes depend on oil prices.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or management cuts its volume guidance.

rows.name: Merck & Co.
rows.thesis: A defensive large drugmaker with low volatility (30%), 5% revenue growth and a 4.3% free-cash-flow yield; it is still above its 200-day average.
rows.risks: GAAP P/E of 140 reflects one-off charges, and the share is down 10% over three months.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or a pipeline or patent setback breaks the earnings path.

rows.name: Nucor
rows.thesis: The leading US steelmaker behind tariff protection: 22% revenue growth, a P/E of 16 and a solid balance sheet; it is holding above its 200-day average.
rows.risks: It is a cyclical stock, and steel prices would fall if industrial demand weakens or tariffs change.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or tariff policy on steel is loosened.

rows.name: CrowdStrike
rows.thesis: The leading cybersecurity platform, with 24% revenue growth and recurring revenue; it is one of the few tech names rising through the selloff (+8.3% over a month, 40% above its 200-day average).
rows.risks: Very high valuation (P/E above 999 on GAAP) and 74% volatility make it vulnerable if the tech selloff reaches software.
rows.exit_if: The share falls back below its 200-day average, or results expected in early December show annual recurring revenue growth slowing sharply.

rows.name: DuPont
rows.thesis: After its breakup, the slimmer DuPont is being re-rated: up 12.9% over a month and 7.7% above its 200-day average, with a 4% free-cash-flow yield.
rows.risks: Thin GAAP margin (4.3%) and a weak 12-month record; the re-rating could stall if industrial demand softens.
rows.exit_if: The share closes below its 200-day average, or the gain over the S&P 500 ETF since purchase falls below +5 points.

rows.name: Marathon Petroleum
rows.thesis: Now my only refiner: P/E of 7.3, 20% free-cash-flow yield and heavy buybacks, while tight fuel supply supports margins.
rows.risks: Refining margins are falling, and the share is down 21% in a month.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 22% above), or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase.

rows.name: Viatris
rows.thesis: A cheap generic-drug maker paying down debt, with a 9.1% free-cash-flow yield; it is 3.5% under its high, and its low volatility suits a defensive role.
rows.risks: High net debt (50% of mcap) and GAAP losses; generic price erosion could return.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or debt reduction stalls.

rows.name: Fortinet
rows.thesis: Network security with a 29% net margin, 20% revenue growth and net cash; after a 31% drawdown, the P/E of about 44 is more reasonable for the quality.
rows.risks: Volatility of 123% shows the market does not trust its growth outlook after the October results.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now only 1% above), or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase.

rows.name: Valero Energy
rows.thesis: A low-cost refiner that returns a lot of cash to shareholders; it rose 9.7% this week.
rows.risks: Fuel demand could weaken or refining margins could shrink.

rows.name: NetApp
rows.thesis: Data storage tied to AI demand at a P/E of 24 with a 4.9% free-cash-flow yield and net cash; Q2 FY27 results are confirmed for December 1.
rows.risks: Hardware stocks are in a sharp selloff, and the share is down 18.6% in a month.
rows.exit_if: Q2 results or guidance disappoint, or it closes below its 200-day average (now 10% above).

rows.name: Morgan Stanley
rows.thesis: Wealth-management fees plus a recovery in dealmaking: 16% revenue growth, a 25.5% margin and a P/E of 14; my only financials holding against a 12.7% index weight.
rows.risks: It is 7% below its 200-day average, and a deeper market drop would hurt trading and deal fees.
rows.exit_if: It falls more than 15% below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 10 points since purchase.

rows.name: Keysight Technologies
rows.thesis: Test and measurement for AI and networking, with 25.5% revenue growth and record orders; fiscal Q4 results are confirmed for after the close on November 19.
rows.risks: A weak fiscal 2027 outlook would add to an 11% gap under its 200-day average during the hardware selloff.
rows.exit_if: The fiscal 2027 outlook implies revenue growth slowing below 10%, or the share keeps falling after results.

rows.name: Illumina, Inc.
rows.thesis: Q3 beat estimates and the company raised guidance, with a 20% margin and net cash; the 22% monthly pullback still leaves the share 16% above its 200-day average.
rows.risks: Revenue growth is only 6%, and the share has not recovered after the November 17 Jefferies talk.
rows.exit_if: It drops below its 200-day average, or trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase.

rows.name: Humana
rows.thesis: Its Medicare Advantage business is recovering after a favorable rate notice; the stock is at a 52-week high with steady momentum.
rows.risks: Medical costs could rise or star ratings could slip.
